messages.subject: confusion about regression operation in CFA
parts:
Hey guys!

I'm now developing a new measurement and want to test its correlation to ability latents in an established model from literature.

The behavioral model is a bi-factor CFA model which has a general factor g, and nested factors vis, cry, spd and mem. All the factors are orthogonal otherwise the model will not converge. 

My confusion raises when I keep the behavior model and regress my measurement, called HB, on to these latents. If I do it separately, means regress only one factor to HB in one model, the estimations are not significant.

Regressions:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
  g ~                                                                   
    HB1               0.023    0.037    0.634    0.526    0.023    0.023

Regressions:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
  spd ~                                                                 
    HB               0.054    0.039    1.391    0.164    0.054    0.054

When I simultaneously regress all the factors on HB, the results can be significant:

Regressions:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
  g ~                                                                   
    HB1              -0.278    0.119   -2.342    0.019   -0.268   -0.267
  vis ~                                                                 
    HB1               0.366    0.197    1.857    0.063    0.344    0.343
  cry ~                                                                 
    HB1               0.707    0.252    2.808    0.005    0.577    0.577
  spd ~                                                                 
    HB1               0.178    0.063    2.823    0.005    0.176    0.175
  mem ~                                                                 
    HB1               0.293    0.135    2.175    0.030    0.281    0.281

But this result is also problematic because all the task measurements I used to construct the latents are positively correlated so the negative estimation of g appears to be weird.

I'm wondering what I did wrong because the two causes are supposed to be similar. If I did not make mistakes which result should I trust?

I appreciate all your valuable suggestions! 

Bests regard.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: confusion about regression operation in CFA
parts: When you use HB1 to predict just one dependent, the other dependents are in the model, yes? But with the potential paths from HB1 constrained to 0? It could be that misspecification (forcing paths to 0 that should not be 0) is biasing the individual coefficient estimates. If this is correct, then you should be seeing evidence of the lack of fit in the fit indices and modification indices for the more limited models. The estimation method is trying to optimize fit overall. In the more limited models, it may be that keeping an estimated path close to 0 minimizes the overall lack of fit when other paths are being forced to 0.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: confusion about regression operation in CFA
parts: Maybe the results is caused by your "all factors orthogonal" model not being best for the data. You indicated that you forced all factors to be orthogonal in order to achieve identification. But that was before adding HB1 as a common predictor, yes? Having this extra (observed?) variable in the model could change the identification situation. Since HB1 predicts all of the other factors in the model, it acts a little bit like a common factor itself, and so now you may have some lack of fit because this almost-common factor model does not match up with the data. Try relaxing the orthogonality constraint among the group factors--allow residual covariance among them--while leaving the constraints in place between the general factor and the group factors. See if that makes the surprising result go away.
